definition: TinyML (short for tiny machine learning) is an area of machine learning that focuses on deploying and running models on low-power, resource-constrained embedded systems such as microcontrollers and edge devices.
details: TinyML supports on-device inference with low latency and minimal reliance on cloud connectivity, which makes it suitable for applications in the Internet of Things (IoT), wearable devices, and real-time systems.

explainer.lead: TinyML deploys and runs machine learning models on low-power, resource-constrained embedded systems such as microcontrollers and edge devices. It matters because it enables on-device inference with low latency and minimal reliance on cloud connectivity.

tiers.eli5: Running tiny smart programs directly on small devices, like a watch or a sensor, instead of sending data to a big computer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for IoT, wearables, and real-time systems where cloud round-trips are too slow or unavailable. Pitfall: tight memory and power budgets force aggressive model compression.
tiers.paperLevel: An area of machine learning focused on deploying and running models on low-power, resource-constrained embedded systems; no formal definition is given.

explainer.example: A wearable detects a gesture by running a small model on its microcontroller, with no network connection.
